open_issues.impact: TRACKED_PROJECT_ENTRIES in policy.py has 6 entries, not 3
open_issues.text: The tracked allowlist is wider than the three entries named in the goal (plans, decisions, project.json): it also keeps legacy-plans, migrations and local-only.json, which the existing migrate and sync code writes and publish-safety already allowed. Dropping them would break migrate and local-only.

open_issues.impact: unknown files directly in projects/<code>/ are blocked at sync --commit, not silently ignored
open_issues.next: owner may ask for a stricter inverted .gitignore
open_issues.text: The allowlist is enforced by the ignore list, doctor (warn on tracked files outside it) and publish-safety PS-PROJECT-LEVEL (block). It is not an inverted .gitignore ('/projects/*/*' with negations), because that would hide unknown files from publish-safety and break existing safety and sync tests.

open_issues.impact: the first sync --commit of an old workspace includes a .gitignore change
open_issues.text: sync --commit now rewrites the policy block of the workspace .gitignore (policy.apply) before it scans and stages. An older workspace therefore gets a .gitignore change in its next sync commit. Behavior change of a public command.

For P3.2: nothing calls set_repo_path or repo_path yet. attach, bind, scan, rebind, detach, project_rows, doctor._bindings, doctor._legacy_plans, integration.check_project and projects.remove still read and write bindings.json. P3.2 must switch them to localconfig (repo.path is one primary path; bindings has many paths per project, so decide what happens to extra checkouts) and then retire bindings.py, workspace-bindings/v1 and the bindings README rows. Layer reading still uses project_config_file(root) = <checkout>/.swissknifeman/config.toml; the new project layer is <ws>/projects/<code>/local/config.toml, so aicore.config.resolve(project=...) and state.backups need the local/ paths (local_backups_dir, local_state_dir are ready). config.toml top level may hold only schema_version and module tables, so [repo] is read as a module table named repo and no module may claim that id.

open_issues.impact: project remove after P3.2 writes local/config.toml
open_issues.text: For P3.2/P3.3: projects.remove treats every file in the project folder as held except project.json and plans/.gitkeep, so a project with a local/ folder is PROJECT_NOT_EMPTY. Decide whether local/ counts as held. doctor._layout accepts local and decisions as project entries; the launcher-only marker <checkout>/.swissknifeman/project.json is unchanged.

For P3.4/P3.5: the layer file is TOML with schema_version and module tables only. Settings such as the optional plans/ and tasks/ links (D5) should be module settings in local/config.toml, not new top-level keys of project-local-config/v1. The schema accepts any module table, so no schema change is needed. SKM_* variables can read repo_path / local_dir through the localconfig helpers.

summary: Added contract project-local-config/v1 (schema, examples, unit.json, README) and aicore.workspace.localconfig (local/ paths, ensure_local, read_local_config, repo_path, set_repo_path, clear_repo_path; new codes PROJECT_LOCAL_CONFIG_INVALID and PROJECT_LOCAL_CONFIG_LOCKED). In the workspace package added policy.py: the tracked allowlist and the ignore list (local/, run files, orch artifacts, model/provider settings, build output) as a managed block of the workspace .gitignore written by init and re-applied by sync --commit before staging, so projects/<code>/local/ is never staged. New doctor check workspace.git-policy; decisions added to the project entries of layout and publish-safety. Tests (test_localconfig, test_policy, updated test_doctor), READMEs and changelogs updated. bindings.json and its API are intentionally unchanged: readers move in P3.2.
